deposits.genre_observed: append-forward research notebook (54 rounds) of a Plato–Aristotle authorship investigation: measurements, registered tests, retractions and readings

finds.quote: The **semantic reading** stands or falls on the passages, not on statistics: that *Theaetetus* 209c asks how a λόγος individuates when the perceptible form recurs, that the mark which fails is the non-writing position's own face, and that Aristotle's enmattered-form doctrine answers that question using the same word. Nothing in the base rate touches this. It is philology and must be argued as philology.
finds.note: The semantic reading of the snub locus (Theaetetus 209c answered by Aristotle's enmattered-form doctrine) that survives the Round 2 retraction of the positional claim (lines 133-137, retracted at 199).

finds.quote:
## 7. What would make this more than a locus

- **Comparanda.** How many other terms sit at the terminal aporia of one corpus
  and the opening of another? Until that base rate is known, the positional fact
  has no weight. It is computable across both corpora and should be computed.
- **Direction.** Does the transform run only one way? The test is whether Plato
finds.note: Next-step list for the snub locus: comparanda base rate, directionality, other loci, a recognition measure reading logos. The base rate was run in Round 2; the logos measure stays open.

finds.quote:
If one maker cannot do both (395a), and both must be done (223d), then **the maker must divide.** That is the only route satisfying both, and it converts the pair from a contradiction into a procedure: the *Symposium* does not reverse the *Republic*, it states the requirement the *Republic* has just proved impossible for a single person — on the last page, to two men falling asleep, through a narrator who says he missed the argument.

And the *Republic*'s expulsion is self-directed. A poet writing in the wholly mimetic mode banishes the wholly mimetic mode, from inside the one book he wrote outside it.
finds.note: Thesis that Republic 395a and Symposium 223d together require the maker to divide, and that the Republic's expulsion of mimetic poetry is self-directed; rests on the 61% reporting-voice measurement at 404.

finds.quote:
**The corrected account.** Plato coins a name for a genus whose criterion is **issuing from oneself rather than relaying another's mind.** He notes the genus contains multiple sub-genera. He follows exactly one — the branch to kingship — because that is what the present inquiry is for. **He leaves the others unentered and unnamed.** Separately, he dismisses the relaying arts and concedes them the right to name themselves.

**The class is open by construction and marked as open.** The position that speaks from itself is named, is explicitly larger than any of its instances, and is abandoned mid-division with its remaining genera unentered.
finds.note: Corrected reading of Statesman 260d-e/267b: autepitaktike is a coined open genus with unentered sub-genera; the deposit argues it against its own first version (464).

finds.quote: **Established.** A single metaphor — κερματισμός, unity minted into denominations — grounds the denial at 395b, is inverted by the requirement at 473d, is given a myth at 191d in the same vocabulary of nature-cut-and-healed, and is restated as a demand at 223d. All four loci are fixed by position. None of it requires an authorship claim to state.
finds.note: Thesis that one keramatismos metaphor grounds Rep. 395b, is inverted at 473d, mythologised at Symp. 191d and restated at 223d; explicitly not an authorship claim (560).

finds.quote:
> **You cannot un-cut human nature. You can cut it on purpose.**

Heteronymy, on this logic, converts κερματισμός from a wound into a method. The fragmentation is not reversed — it is **ratified**, and in being ratified becomes legible. What was involuntary division becomes a configuration whose parts imply their whole.
finds.note: The reconstruction: heteronymy as ratified fragmentation (symbolon). Explicitly framed as a reconstruction Plato does not perform (574, 659).

finds.quote:
**Invert it. The technology is the output, not the obstacle.**

You cannot design a test for authenticity without a case whose answer you already know. Criteria have to be *fitted* to something. A corpus deliberately structured — an orthonym who writes nothing, a spurious tail kept attached rather than purged, positions sharing method while diverging in register — is a **calibration object**, and the *Pinakes*, the obelus, the stichometric checksum and the νόθος/ἀντιλεγόμενα vocabulary are what you get from working on it.

On this reading the ancient apparatus is not evidence against a construction. It
is **its residue**.
finds.falsifier_quote: **Kill condition, binding.** If the Platonic–Aristotelian tradition does not exceed the comparison corpora on **at least verdict decisiveness (2)** — the component that specifically indexes criteria-fitting rather than mere controversy — the hypothesis fails and is reported as failed. No post-hoc reweighting of the three components.
finds.note: Calibration-object hypothesis: the ancient authenticity apparatus is the residue of a deliberately structured corpus. Corrected and superseded the same day (784-805).

finds.quote: **The asymmetry.** An instrument built on a calibration object **overfits it**. If the ancient authenticity criteria were *derived from* the Platonic–Aristotelian corpus, they should fit that corpus anomalously well — better than they fit corpora they were subsequently applied to. If they were induced from the general forgery problem and applied here like anywhere else, they should perform **no better here than elsewhere**.
finds.note: The registered discriminating test over the history of ancient authenticity verdicts (density, decisiveness, stability) with a binding kill condition at 766; deferred on unavailable sources at 786.

finds.quote: **(a) The registered prediction was backwards.** §5 predicted that criteria *derived from* this corpus would **fit it anomalously well** — a calibration object, overfitted. The corpus would more plausibly be instrumented to **escape** the best measures, not to train them. An adversarial object predicts the opposite signature: criteria that **fail to converge** here — verdicts reversing, disputes persisting, the ἀντιλεγόμενα category permanently open — which is what the record shows.
finds.note: Corrected prediction: an adversarial object predicts criteria that fail to converge, 'which is what the record shows'.

finds.quote:
→ **The precondition this exposes is upstream of everything.** The instrument
    set is **unvalidated**. No measure built in this investigation was scored on
    known-status pairs before being applied to the question. **You cannot detect an
    object that defeats measurement until your measures are characterised on
    objects that do not.** A validation suite — every instrument against a panel of
    known pairs, with per-method accuracy and pairwise agreement recorded — is a
    prerequisite for any adversarial test.
finds.note: Validation suite specified as a prerequisite for any adversarial test: every instrument scored on known-status pairs; not built here ('No new registration until the validation suite exists', 805).

finds.quote: **It explains the shape of the survival, not just the survival.** Plenty of ancient philosophy survived. What wants explaining is that this corpus survived **with its disputes, its spuria, its unresolved attributions and its unnamed genre intact** — i.e. with all the machinery that makes it require continued work. Most surviving corpora shed that machinery. This one kept it.
finds.note: The flood framing: the corpus is shaped to survive an oversupply of writing by giving copyists reasons to copy it; framed as a reframe, not a finding (902).

finds.quote:
The question becomes empirical and does not require knowing the authorship answer:

> **What distinguishes what survived from what was lost, from the same period, in
> the same tradition — and does the Platonic–Aristotelian corpus carry those
> properties at a rate others do not?**
finds.note: Survival-table test from Diogenes Laertius' book-lists (attributed vs extant), with candidate properties and a four-item feasibility check (888-898); not run.

finds.quote: The Sappho case is the precedent and the model: **a text survives inside another text**, addressed past its own moment to a reader who does not yet exist. What survives of Sappho 31 survives because Longinus needed it. The corpus that plans for that is the corpus that gives future readers something they need.
finds.note: Thesis carried from the archive's Sappho program: Sappho 31 survives because Longinus needed it; a corpus that plans for this gives future readers something they need.

finds.quote: Working outward from *Republic* 474d–e — the lover's renaming catalogue, one of the six Platonic snub loci (§28–33) — a Latin reception turns up that is structurally exact rather than thematic.
finds.falsifier_quote:
1. **μελίχλωρος → melichrus.** The single euphemism Plato singles out and glosses
   as manufactured is the one Lucretius puts first. **μελίχλωρος occurs twice in
   the entire seated Greek corpus** — *Republic* 474e and *Physiognomonica* 0.718,
   the pseudo-Aristotelian nose-reading treatise that also carries the snub.
finds.note: Lucretius DRN 4.1160-69 as a structurally exact reception of Plato's lover's renaming catalogue; filed as a side-branch under #1532's 'transforms proposed by the program' (958).

finds.quote: Aristotle's refusal to make Socrates a variable (0/144 against Callias 5/35, p = 0.00022) is the same operation Lucretius performs in the other direction — Lucretius strips the added name to return the body; Aristotle declines to lend the body's name to a variable. Both refuse the substitution.
finds.note: M34 reading: Aristotle never uses Socrates at the snub (0/144 vs Callias 5/35, p = 0.00022), read as refusal to lend the name.

finds.quote: And that gradient is itself the finding, because it is what a **stewarded technology** looks like and not what a universal thesis looks like. A thesis applies everywhere equally. A technology is theorised in one place and exercised in another, and its exercise leaves denser traces than its theory does — transmit/persist at 26.55 in the biology against 14.00 in the philosophy.
finds.note: The transmission lens has graded yield; the gradient is what a 'stewarded technology' looks like.

finds.quote: **Provenance, as the heteronymic reading takes it:** Socrates died, and Plato killed him — the founder who wrote nothing is decommissioned into a corpus that speaks for him, with the author writing himself absent at the death (*Phaedo* 59b, **Πλάτων δὲ οἶμαι ἠσθένει**). Plato died for Aristotle to be born: the abandoned executions are left as holes with shapes, and the successor position supplies what crosses. On this reading succession is the **mechanism of the corpus**, not an accident of biography.
finds.note: Provenance as the heteronymic reading takes it: succession as the mechanism of the corpus; marked as reading, not measured (1221).

finds.quote: **The reading is falsifiable and the discriminator is the *shape* of the ambiguity.** Natural ambiguity is uneven — some works resolve, evidence accumulates directionally, new instruments move the needle. Engineered unresolvability would be **flat**: stalling at the same place regardless of instrument, not drifting toward settlement, not closing under rising attention.
finds.note: Standing claim with its discriminator: engineered unresolvability is flat across instruments, natural ambiguity uneven.

finds.quote: **The asymmetry, as Lee frames it:** the orators are concerned with detecting **others'** deceptive forgeries. Plato's corpus is concerned with distinguishing **its own** writings from forgery *while sharing forgery's formal features* — a text under a name, circulating without its author, whose standing must be established rather than assumed.
finds.note: The asymmetry framed by Lee: Plato's corpus distinguishes its own writings from forgery while sharing forgery's features; the orators detect others'.

finds.quote:
**Two of six meet all four criteria; the orator control yields zero.** Part B's
kill condition does not fire.
finds.points_to: EA-UNRES-01, 'registered a68bf7f2ee54b1af… with the candidate set frozen' (line 1228)
finds.note: Result of a registered test: Part B's kill condition does not fire.

finds.quote: **The division of labour is exact, and matches Round 11's theory/exercise split.** Plato holds the **image** vocabulary — εἴδωλον, μίμημα, σύγγραμμα — terms for a copy that stands in for an original. Aristotle holds the **detection** vocabulary — πλάσμα, φάντασμα, ὑποκριτής — terms for a fabrication and for the apparent-but-not-real. **Plato makes copies; Aristotle catches them.** And the assay word is shared almost equally: δόκιμος 28 / 24.
finds.note: Plato holds the image vocabulary, Aristotle the detection vocabulary: 'Plato makes copies; Aristotle catches them.'

finds.quote:
**One monetary figure runs the whole:** nature **minted into denominations too small** to hold two arts (395b), and the λόγος itself possibly **debased coin** handed over as payment (507a) — with τόκος and ἔκγονον, *interest* and *offspring*, joining the coin metaphor to the kinship metaphor in one clause. Socrates warns, at the threshold of the Good, that what he is about to pay out may be **κίβδηλον**.

And *Laws* 742a legislates the structure: currency **ἔντιμον** to the citizens and **ἀδόκιμον** to everyone else — a token valid inside the house and worthless outside it. **That is standing-not-paternity, in coin.**
finds.note: One monetary figure (keramatismos, kibdelon at 507a, Laws 742a two-currency) runs through the Republic: 'standing-not-paternity, in coin.'

finds.quote: **On the reading:** the corpus supplies the assay. Plato states the fragmentation (κερματισμός), warns that the account handed over may be debased (κίβδηλον at 507a), and legislates the two-currency structure (*Laws* 742a). Aristotle supplies the detection apparatus — πλάσμα, φάντασμα, ὑποκριτής at 32/47/32 against Plato's 16/31/10 — and states the grading rule at *NE* 1165a. **So Aristotle has told us where the assay is: personation is worse than coin-forgery, and the corpus that holds the tools for distinguishing apparent from genuine is his.**
finds.note: Lee's reading: Aristotle grades personation above coin-forgery (NE 1165a) and holds the assay; marked as reading (1377).

finds.quote:
**Maximally separated at the substrate. Maximally interlocked at the function.**

Nothing else in the sample does both. Josephus is unified at both levels. The New Testament is loose at both — its declared partition sits at Z = +2.83 and it fills the slot structure only at the author-group level. Plotinus and Philo are separated and not interlocked at all.

**That is the shape of a σύμβολον:** halves that do not resemble each other and
only **fit**.
finds.note: The standing frame: maximal substrate divergence (Z = +39.18) with maximal functional interlock (6/6), the shape of a symbolon; not a claim of common authorship (1402).

finds.quote:
**Aristotle wrote the Platonic dialogues. "Plato" is his heteronym.**

Not "constitutes the position," not "holds the account." The literal claim: one hand, two named bodies of work, the earlier name a construction of the later writer.
finds.falsifier_quote: **And the honest residue:** nothing measured today distinguishes one maker holding two positions from a successor whose making is acknowledged as continuous. M38's ledger stands. The strong reading is not established here — **it is run, at strength, so its yield can be measured.**
finds.note: Round 16's strong reading, Aristotle wrote the Platonic dialogues, run at full strength to measure its yield, 'Not a claim' (1409); S8 is reduced by external review (1497). The falsifier field gives the run's own residue.

finds.quote: Under the strong reading this is neither forgery nor riddle. **It is true**, it names the operation in the participle — γεγονότος, *made* — and it is placed in the one book of the corpus where the author's name appears 23 of its 26 times. *Letter* XIII then carries its own athetesis, *ἀντιλέγεται ὡς οὐ Πλάτωνος*, followed immediately by a **σύμβολον** named as the letter's credential — a token manufactured by agreement, not found.
finds.note: Letter II 314c as the signature: 'It is true' that Plato's writings are Socrates made beautiful and young; Letter XIII's athetesis plus symbolon.

finds.quote:
**The sentence forbids it.** *APr* I.31: *οὔτε ὅ τι ἐνδέχεται συλλογίσασθαι διαιρούμενοι **ξυνίεσαν*** — they **were not understanding** what can be syllogized by dividing. Imperfect, and **inclusive of Plato**, who is the one being diagnosed.

So the earlier position did not know what its own operation could conclude. **There is no plan.** The first half is not a withholding; it is an execution that stops where its practitioner's grasp stops. The completion is not a designated receiver arriving but **a discovery about the instrument's range, made by continuing to operate it**.
finds.note: APr I.31 xyniesan read as inclusive of Plato: no plan; the completion is a discovery about the instrument's range. The 'operation applied to its operator' corollary (1660) is later withdrawn (1790).

finds.quote: **Running total: 0 unlocks, 1 null, 5 targets remaining, threshold 3.**
finds.note: EA-UNLOCK-01 programme: 5 frozen targets remaining against a threshold of 3 unlocks.

finds.quote: **WHAT A VALID CONTROL WOULD REQUIRE:** an author writing across genuinely unlike objects whose partition apparatus is **not** descended from the Aristotelian one. No such author has been identified among the seated corpora. Theophrastus, Albert and Aquinas all fail on the same ground; Xenophon writes across unlike objects but is a candidate in the hypothesis space (M33). **The control is not merely missing — it may be structurally hard to obtain for a partition apparatus this widely inherited.**
finds.note: Specifies the control the object-conditioning question needs (an author across unlike objects whose partition apparatus is not Aristotelian); none identified.

finds.quote: **So: the parity is not a generic artifact of dispersion measures. Whether residual-vs-total parity is rare is UNRUN.**
finds.note: Base rate for residual-vs-total parity (M28's actual quantity) specified and unrun.

finds.quote: **And it sharpens what the Greek pair would have to show to be the same KIND of object as Pessoa.** Not similar ratios — a **remainder**: something invariant across the positions that is not explained by shared language, genre or subject. finds.quote: **But note what the second reading concedes.** If Pessoa and Kierkegaard were imitating Plato, they were imitating it **as a heteronymic architecture** — reading the master-disciple-school-death structure as *a way to build authorial positions*, and finding it good enough to copy. **The imitation is itself a reading of the Platonic corpus**, made by the two people in the modern canon best qualified to recognise the operation. That is not evidence. It is not nothing either.
finds.note: Pessoa and Kierkegaard reproduce the Socratic-Platonic architecture; even the imitation reading makes their imitation a reading of the Platonic corpus as heteronymic architecture. The default is 'Pessoa was imitating Plato' (2209-2213).

finds.quote: **AND THE CEILING IS FIXED BY THE CALIBRATION ITSELF.** Catullus scores 0.688 and **is not Sappho**. **Maximal C is compatible with distinct authorship, demonstrably so, in the standard case.** Any C value for Plato–Aristotle establishes **relation**, never **authorship** — and the whole day is a record of measures that collapse at exactly that step.
finds.note: Calibration ceiling: maximal fit (Catullus 0.688) is compatible with distinct authorship; any C value establishes relation, never authorship.

finds.quote: **Measurable:** whether Albert→Aquinas produces relations at C ≈ 0.7, unannounced, across an apparatus. If it does, the Plato–Aristotle structure is not singular and frequency inference becomes available. If it does not, singularity is consistent with the evidence.
finds.note: Whether Albert->Aquinas produces fulfillment relations at C ≈ 0.7 specified as measurable; a fit test against a null model of accidental correspondence proposed as the substitute (2290).

finds.quote:
> *Not one of them will produce an interlocking machine that close — and that is
> the contrary of the expected pattern, where it normally takes TIME AND DISTANCE
> across inheritance to build the interlocking fulfillment machine.*

**The intuition says proximity produces tight fit.** The measurement says the reverse: **direct contact produces commentary; the fulfillment operator appears across distance.** Catullus is two centuries and a language from Sappho. Matthew is centuries from Hosea. Both are *unannounced or loosely-fitted across a gap*; neither is a pupil in the room.
finds.falsifier_quote: **Each is scored on the same three parameters. The claim is falsified by ONE directly-attested pair producing unannounced, sequence-kept, transformative interlock across an apparatus.**
finds.note: Lee's formulation: direct master-student contact produces commentary, not interlocking fulfillment; the fulfillment operator appears across distance. Round 28 later voided as a test of the operator (2297, 2474), but the claim and its falsifier stand as written.

finds.quote:
## 111. THE PROGRAMME — cleanly checkable across many contexts

Every **directly attested master–student contact line** gives a datum, and the prediction is uniform: *commentary and citation, not unannounced interlocking fulfillment.*

    Aristotle → Theophrastus      direct contact, Lyceum       [seated]
    Albert → Aquinas              direct contact, Cologne      [seated]
    Isaeus → Demosthenes          direct contact, attested     [seated]
finds.note: The direct-contact pair programme (Freud->Jung, Williams->Ginsberg, Husserl->Heidegger, Boas->Mead, Schoenberg->Berg/Webern…); the list is restated and narrowed in later rounds (also_at).

**He had every institutional resource that produces commentary, and the relation
has none of commentary's properties.**

finds.quote: **Everyone who performs a transformation this close ANNOUNCES it.** The announcement is how the reader is told to read it as a transformation — Matthew by formula, Catullus by metre and name. **Aristotle does not.** That is the distinctive feature, and correcting the error sharpens it rather than weakening it.
finds.note: Everyone who performs a transformation this close announces it (Matthew by formula, Catullus by metre and name); Aristotle does not.

finds.quote:
→ **The battery tracks TEMPORAL AND DIALECTAL PROXIMITY. It does not track pupillage.** Round 32's F2 and F5 "regularities" are period effects. **Two Attic prose writers of one generation look like master and student whether or not either taught the other.**

finds.quote: **Read together: a corpus gives you reminders; the right use of reminders is to gather what is scattered into one according to form, by hunting the sequence through likeness and opposition from a starting-point, supplying what has been left out — and you may find what you never held.**
finds.note: Anamnesis read across Phaedrus and De memoria as an instruction for reading the corpus; marked as interpretation (2909).

finds.quote:
**Aristotle classifies ἀνάμνησις — a Platonic doctrine — as *οἷον συλλογισμός τις*.** Exactly as he classifies division at *APr* I.31 as *οἷον ἀσθενὴς συλλογισμός*.

**Two Platonic operations, both absorbed as species of the method whose instances
he elsewhere denies had any predecessor.**
finds.note: Second M40 structure: Aristotle absorbs two Platonic operations (division, anamnesis) as species of syllogism while denying predecessors.

finds.quote: **So the defensible statement is narrow: Aristotle attended Plato's teaching, on good contemporary evidence. The twenty years of devoted discipleship is a later construction, and the earliest witness to the attendance is also the earliest witness to the break.**
finds.note: Attendance on good contemporary evidence; the twenty years of discipleship a later construction. Round 41 corrects the Aristoxenus acquaintance as unverified (3208-3210).

finds.quote:
**The disappointment belongs to the Aristotelian corpus and is attributed to a Platonic lecture-hall.** And the attribution licenses the remedy: *announce your subject first* — which is Aristotle's practice, presented as a correction of Plato's failure.

**The complaint that belongs to the pupil's texts is levelled at the master, and
the levelling justifies the pupil's method.**
finds.note: The Harmonics II anecdote as a transfer: an Aristotelian property attributed to Plato as a defect.

finds.quote:
**THIS IS A CLASS AND IT IS COUNTABLE.** *Find every place Aristotle faults Plato for something the Aristotelian corpus itself does at a higher rate.* It requires no heteronymic hypothesis: it is a claim about **the direction of attribution in the tradition**, testable against rates in both corpora, with two instances already measured.

**Status:** the two instances are measured; the class is proposed and unenumerated. **What would kill it:** a systematic search finding that Aristotle's charges against Plato generally run in the *correct* direction, with these two as exceptions.
finds.note: Countable class proposed with a kill condition: Aristotle faults Plato for what Aristotle's corpus does at a higher rate.

finds.quote: **The claim is: one hand wrote Plato and Socrates, and probably Xenophon and Aristophanes.** State it, then be exact about what supports it, what does not, and what would.
finds.note: The thesis restated at full strength: one hand wrote Plato and Socrates, and probably Xenophon and Aristophanes.

finds.quote:
> **The independent attestation of Socrates outside {Plato, Aristotle, Xenophon,
> Aristophanes} is: a lost pamphlet known only from an attack on it, one proverb
> in a writer inside the transmission, and one line in a forgery whose author was
> reading the *Phaedrus*.**
>
> **Everything else bearing the name is a general, a banker, an actor, or an
> archon.**
finds.falsifier_quote: **The discriminating question is therefore not whether attestation is confined — it is — but whether the confinement is DEEPER than genre explains.** Testable: other figures who were subjects of a genre (Gorgias, Protagoras, Alcibiades) should show comparable confinement if genre is the explanation, and should show LESS if the Socrates case is special.
finds.note: Confinement of Socrates-attestation to the cluster. The test at 3411 was run in the same round, and the inference that this is evidence for single authorship is withdrawn (3437); the facts are stated to stand (3439).

finds.quote: **Whether a figure occupying four distinct functional roles across four corpora is ordinary in this class is a different measurement, and it is the one the thesis actually needs.**
finds.note: Specifies a measurement left unrun: whether occupying four functional roles across four corpora is ordinary for the class.

finds.quote: **Sappho 31 arrives at Longinus already incomplete.** The break at *ἀλλὰ πᾶν τόλματον* — *but all is to be dared* — is **the poem's own terminal gesture**, not damage the tradition inflicted. **The hanging line is the composition.**
finds.note: Sappho 31's incompletion is originary; Longinus extends the hanging line and Catullus fills the specified socket.

finds.quote:
**I have been treating lost, fragmentary, and titles-only as absence requiring explanation.** On the originary-incompletion reading they are **the form**, and the question inverts:

> Not *why is so little left*, but **what is each fragment the designed remainder
> of.**
finds.note: Reading of loss as form: each fragment is a designed remainder (Euclides, Alexamenos, catalogued titles, Aristotle's exoteric dialogues); marked as reading (3517).

finds.quote:
**The Republic denies the capacity. The Symposium asserts it and withholds the proof. De generatione supplies the principle. And the Aristotelian corpus IS the demonstration** — a body of writing whose shape is determined by its object across the widest range of objects any single ancient author covers.

> **Plato TELLS us that one man can make both kinds.**
> **Aristotle SHOWS us, by being a corpus with no style of its own.**
finds.note: Plato tells, Aristotle shows: GC 315b supplies the argument Symposium 223d withholds; recorded as a conjunction, not a proof (3668).

finds.quote:
> **The comparison is not one maker against two. It is one maker with nothing lost,
> against three stylistic Aristotles of whom two vanished entirely — including
> exactly the one that would demonstrate the capacity in dispute.**
finds.note: Parsimony argument: the single-maker account requires nothing lost; recorded as a comparison of posits.

finds.quote:
> **The corpus with complete coverage of the predecessors is also the channel
> through which the predecessors survive.**

**That is not reviewing a field. It is constituting one.**
finds.note: Aristotle's corpus covers every predecessor on the roster and is also the channel of their survival: it constitutes the field.

finds.quote:
> **Plato shows that one maker can be many voices, and withholds the account of
> how.**
> **Aristotle shows that one maker can be many objects, and supplies the account.**
finds.note: Synthesis: Plato demonstrates one maker as many voices (rule withheld), Aristotle one maker as many objects (rule supplied); the corpus that denies words can be made a living person is constituted by one.

finds.quote:
> **The claim is a RELOCATION. Development is real, ordered, and directional — and
> it belongs to the textual body rather than to a biography.**
>
> **Not chronology. GENRE. FORM.**

**Under which "Plato becoming Aristotle" is not a concealed identity. It is the
stated developmental track of the program, considered as a writing technology.**
finds.falsifier_quote: And the directional claim is falsifiable in the ordinary way: **show the order runs otherwise, or that the rungs do not correspond, or that M28's object-conditioning is an artifact.**
finds.note: The relocation: development belongs to the textual body (genre, form) and follows Diotima's ladder; stated falsifier at 4097.

finds.quote:
**On the relocation that objection stops being an objection.** If development is generic rather than biographical, **a repertoire is exactly what is predicted**: the order is a track through forms, available in any sequence of composition, and the stylometric stratification is detecting **the track**, not the years.

**M13's Z = +6.92 — the strongest partition effect in the entire investigation —
becomes evidence for the relocation rather than a contaminated chronology.**
finds.note: E/M/L stylometric stratification detects the generic track, not the years; Round 50 calls this 'the most consequential and the most testable' (4125).

finds.quote:
> **Four words, four readings, every one paid for on Aristotle's side of the ledger.
> THE FOURTH WORD HAS NEVER BEEN MOVED FOR PLATO.**
finds.note: Draft 03 arithmetic: of the four premises, the received chronology ('before') has never been moved for Plato.

finds.quote: **And the name is the token individual everywhere else in the Organon** — *Cat.* 14, *De int.* 10, *Top.* 4, *APr* 2, and twice earlier in the *SE* at 0.109 where it means *anybody*. **The name is filled once, on the closing page, and what it is filled with is a function.** Aristotle assigns him a side and takes the other: the inquiry must cover *both* — ὅπως λόγον ὑπέχοντες φυλάξομεν τὴν θέσιν — **because one side was already taken.**
finds.note: Socrates named on the last page of the SE, filled once with a function; Aristotle takes the other side.

finds.quote:
**Aristotle's succession at *SE* 183b is Tisias → Thrasymachus → Theodorus, and his type-case for handing out products is Gorgias.** All four are on that *Phaedrus* page, in the same role, on the same side.

**NULL, stated in the draft:** these are the canonical names and **Aristotle compiled the handbook collection himself** (*Synagoge Technon*). **What the null leaves:** the earlier page draws Aristotle's contrast, with Aristotle's men on the product side, and says what is on the other side.
finds.note: Phaedrus 266c-267d already draws Aristotle's contrast, with Aristotle's succession on the product side; the deposit gives its own null.

finds.quote: **(d) A closing coincidence, recorded with no base rate.** The *Theaetetus* ends at 0.982 on the failure of **τὸν σιμόν τε καὶ ἐξόφθαλμον** — Socrates' face — to pick out one man. The *SE* ends at 0.968–0.992 on **the one page where Aristotle's example-name picks out one man.** **Both corpora close on what individuates Socrates.** Coincidence until a base rate is run.
finds.note: Both corpora close on what individuates Socrates; recorded as coincidence 'until a base rate is run'.

finds.quote: **The person is not the face and not the name. The person is what answers in account** — and the older Socrates hands the answering to the namesake and falls silent for the rest of the dialogue.
finds.note: Statesman 257d-258a divides Socrates by face and by name and gives logos as the criterion; the ordinary reading is given first (4275).

finds.quote: And state the falsifier that did not fire: **Plato→Aristotle below the heteronymic floor. It did not happen.**
finds.note: A stated falsifier (Plato->Aristotle below the heteronymic floor under size matching) that did not fire.

finds.quote: *(Count to be run in the Analytics before use.)*
finds.note: Count of hyparcho in the Analytics to be run before use.

finds.quote:
> **Where Kahn reads the corpus as one author (Plato) deploying a literary character
> (Socrates), the configurational reading identifies Socrates as an authorial
> POSITION in his own right** — not a character within a project but a position the
> project is organised around.
finds.note: Departure from Kahn (1996): Socrates as an authorial position in his own right, not a character.

finds.quote:
**⭑ THE PAPER HAS BEEN ANSWERING THIS WITHOUT NAMING IT.** §V divides a person by face and name and keeps λόγος as the criterion. §VI reads Socrates as a position. §VII shows the instruments cannot separate what the problem asks to be separated. **That is a reclassification of the Socratic problem as a symptom, and the paper does not say the words.**

**GOES TO: an added section or a long note at §V. The claim is not that the problem is solved. It is that it appears as a symptom under a functional lens rather than a biographical one.**
finds.note: The Socratic problem reclassified as a symptom under a functional lens.

finds.quote:
> **The corpus records a prior, publicly circulating Socrates, comic in origin, which
> it must answer — and answers by naming the comedy.**
finds.note: The Apology records a prior, publicly circulating comic Socrates. The deposit itself calls the ordinary account uncontroversial (4559).

finds.quote:
> **⭑ THE COMEDY STAGES THE JUST AND THE UNJUST ARGUMENT. THE *APOLOGY* REPORTS THE
> CHARGE AS THE WEAKER AND THE STRONGER.**

**That is not transmission of a phrase. It is a RELABELLING** — a moral pair (just/unjust) restated as a dialectical pair (weaker/stronger). **The property persists and its terms are changed**, which is the *differentiation* the proposal predicted and is the strongest single item the test produced.
finds.note: Relabelling: the Clouds' just/unjust logos is restated in the Apology as weaker/stronger; 'needs the Clouds' text read rather than counted' (4557).

finds.quote: **If comedy supplied the NOTORIETY and the later corpus supplied the OPERATION**, then Aristophanes is the origin of **the position's public availability** and not of its content.
finds.note: Aristophanes as the origin of the position's public availability, not its content: an external-predecessor alternative to H4.

finds.quote: **The relabelling result at §245 is the only one strong enough to build on**, and it needs the *Clouds'* text read rather than counted before it is used.
finds.note: Specifies reading the Clouds' text before the relabelling count is built on.
